title: API config runtime sketch - Jamie
content:
Top-level goal: sketch runtime-facing part of API config that lives in customer config and is consumed by serving runtime and control plane. This is a brain-dump / working doc. Rough, intentionally loose.

Context / constraints:
- Needs to express: model variant, preferred quantization profile, batching hints, cache policy, fallback/model_families, latency vs cost preference.
- Must be simple for product teams to reason about; runtime will fill gaps with defaults.
- Backwards compatible with current minimal config (model + concurrency).

High-level fields (starter idea):
- model: string (required)  # e.g. rdx/llama2-70b-qat
- variant: string (optional) # e.g. low-latency, cost-optimized (maps to kernel selection + sequence optimizations)
- quant_profile: string (optional) # e.g. fp16, int8-q4, int8-q4f 
- batching: single string descriptor (enabled,max_batch_size,max_wait_ms,priority) e.g. "enabled=true;max_batch_size=64;max_wait_ms=12;priority=normal"
- cache_policy: single string descriptor (type,ttl_ms,max_items) e.g. "prefix,600000,50000"
- fallback_policies: comma-separated list of compatible model ids/variants to fall back to
- routing: lightweight CSV for regions and tiers e.g. "us-west1|eu-west1;hosted|dedicated"

Note: the shapes above are for human thinking. Implementation will be YAML/JSON. Keep the customer-facing config small.

Runtime interpretation notes (how serving runtime should use fields):
- quant_profile: runtime maps to prebuilt kernel and memory layout. If model binary not available in exact quant profile, try nearest compatible and update logs.
- batching.max_wait_ms: soft SLO for max latency before executing smaller batch. For high-priority traffic we should have max_wait_ms <= 8ms.
- batching.priority: used by router to favor smaller allocations for critical routes.
- cache_policy.prefix: if prefix caching enabled, store KV-cache entries for identical request prefixes up to ttl_ms. Prefix equality should be hashed using canonicalized prompt.

Open questions / design decisions:
- Should quant_profile be prescriptive (force only that profile) or advisory (preferred)? Proposal: advisory with a boolean enforce_quant true/false. Default false.
- How to express multi-model rollouts (canary traffic split)? Keep rollout config separate per route (console/rollouts). This config should include a field 'compatible_with_rollout': true/false.
- How to represent prompt templates / function calling metadata? Probably outside runtime-config; kept in route-level spec.

Sketch: lightweight example config (YAML-like)

---
model: rdx/llama2-70b
variant: low-latency
quant_profile: int8-q4f
enforce_quant: false
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_size: 64
  max_wait_ms: 12
  priority: normal
cache_policy:
  type: prefix
  ttl_ms: 600000  # 10 minutes
  max_items: 50000
fallback_policies:
  - rdx/llama2-70b-qat
  - rdx/llama2-70b-8bit
routing:
  regions: [us-west1, eu-west1]
  tiers: [hosted, dedicated]
---

Runtime flow ASCII (very rough):

Client -> API Gateway -> Router -> (Select route + model variant) -> Runtime queue -> Batcher -> Executor (GPU) -> Postprocess -> Client
                              |                                                ^
                              |-> Cache (prefix/kvcache) -----------------------|

Key operational signals to surface in console for this config:
- effective quant_profile (actual used)
- batch sizes histogram (per route)
- average and p95 wait_ms in batcher
- cache hit/miss ratio, cold-start misses
- fallback activations (count/time)

Compatibility and edge cases:
- If batching.enabled = false but route has high concurrency, runtime should still do micro-batching at kernel level where beneficial (tunable flag). Must document difference between "user batching" and "runtime micro-batching".
- If fallback list is empty -> fail open to run with closest compatible model, but log and alert (config validation step).
- For private deployments, enforce_quant true might be required for compliance reasons (customer-managed binaries).

TODOs / next steps:
- [ ] Run quick validation script to ensure new fields parse with existing control-plane (RDW-2345).
- [ ] Add example in hosted-api quickstart and test behavior with real traffic. (assign: Casey)
- [ ] Spec for console UI to select quant profile + explain tradeoffs (assign: Olivia)
- [ ] Short doc mapping quant_profile -> kernel families + expected memory / latency impact (owner: Jamie)

Loose notes / heuristics for default values:
- default max_batch_size: 32 for >8k token models, 64 otherwise (need benchmarks).
- default max_wait_ms: 10ms for low-latency tier, 40ms for cost-optimized tier.
- default cache ttl: 5-15m depending on user workload.

Questions to discuss on call:
- enforce_quant: default false, but rampable via account policy? pros/cons.
- Should "batching.priority" be exposed in public API or only via console?
- How to validate fallback compatibility automatically? (signature check, architecture check)

Notes-to-self: copy sections into a clean PR template after polishing. Link to existing api-config-design-scratchpad-jamie.json and runtime-draft-samir-patel for cross-ref.

End of scratchpad.

-- Jamie
